newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: ASEAN to tell new members don't quarrel with guns.
newsitem.headline: ASEAN to tell new members don't quarrel with guns.

text.p: ASEAN will tell prospective members Burma, Laos and Cambodia they can criticise each other but should not resort to guns, Philippine Foreign Secretary Domingo Siazon said on Monday.
"We will talk to them and say, 'Don't quarrel with guns. You can go through the process, you can criticise each other, but no assassination'," Siazon told reporters.

Foreign ministers of the ASEAN (Association of South East Asian Nations) decided in Kuala Lumpur last weekend they would admit the three countries in July, resisting opposition by some Western powers critical of Burma's human right s record.

"The chairman of the ASEAN standing committee will see if democratic reforms are under way," Siazon said. Malaysia is currently chairman of the committee but is scheduled to relinquish the post to the Philippines in July.

Commenting on reported reservations by some members about admitting all three countries now, Siazon said: "Consensus does not mean all of you are strongly for it. You may have reservation but it's not strong enough to block. It's not a veto right."
ASEAN has traditionally decided on issues not by a formal vote but informally by consensus among members, which are the Philippines, Malaysia, Indonesia, Singapore, Thailand, Vietnam and Brunei.
